title: Debt collector is at your door
body: A man in a white shirt says he's from Maxfield Recovery Services. Bigga sold them the rest of your debt. You owe it plus two years of interest. He has a printed sheet. If you don't settle today he'll be back with paperwork and a witness. He looks like he means it.

title: Your ex is now your competition
body: Word moves through the community: your ex started their own business. Same market, same neighbourhood. Miss Enid says they have six regular clients already. When you built together they had access to your whole operation.

choices.label: Let them run. The market is big enough.
Move to a different part of the market.

title: InsureFirst declines your application
body: Email from InsureFirst Commercial Insurance: 'Following a credit and tenancy history check, we are unable to offer business insurance at this time. A prior eviction on record is a disqualifying factor under our current underwriting rules.'

choices.label: Find a smaller insurer who doesn't check history.
Wait six months and reapply elsewhere.

title: Deja texts again — different tone
body: It's been a year since you said no. She texts: 'I know you're busy. I'm not asking for me anymore. Just for the books I need. It's $35.' The 'just' is doing a lot of work in that sentence. So is the year of silence.

title: NCB offers to refinance your loan
body: Email from National Commercial Bank: they can consolidate your existing loan at a lower rate if your account is in good standing. The new terms cut your weekly payment by $12. The process takes two weeks and costs $50 in processing fees.

choices.label: Refinance with NCB. Lower weekly cost.
